A1.justification: Despite the rename from SteeringControl to SteeringSafety, both PDFs describe the same benchmark and modular steering framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original steering experiments on Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, including aggregate results in Figure 2 and dataset-level results under three steering settings in Figures 3–8.

after.justification: V3 retains original steering evaluations and adds experiments on Gemma and smaller Qwen models, morality steering, long-context reasoning, and human agreement with automated judges.

M1.justification: The evaluated direction-generation, grid-search, and intervention procedures remain the same for DIM, ACE, CAA, PCA, and LAT, including CAST conditional steering. V3 expands their mathematical and implementation descriptions. V1's optional COSMIC-selector paragraph disappears, but both versions use GridSearch in every evaluated method; its omission does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V3 adds a distinct long-context reasoning scenario using LongBench v2 and directly steers commonsense morality, which v1 explicitly treats only as an unsteered secondary task. These extend both input conditions and intervention objectives. The nine-perspective terminology otherwise largely reorganizes existing coverage rather than introducing nine new tasks.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate DIM, ACE, CAA, PCA, and LAT against unsteered models. Standard, NoKL, and Conditional variants already appear in v1. The added evaluations retain this comparator set; the unavailable DIM refusal result on Gemma reflects failed KL filtering in a newly added model setting.

E3.justification: V3 expands the evaluated model configurations from two to five and replaces substring matching with likelihood scoring for TwinViews, restoring political-view evaluation for Llama. It revises the entanglement normalization and introduces a LongBench protocol using 180 examples, contexts up to 32k tokens, bf16, FlashAttention-2, and likelihood scoring. Most smaller dataset counts in Table 3 document v1's existing 20% subsampling, although refusal split counts also differ.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained KL-filter and conditional-steering comparisons, v3 adds model-scale consistency analysis, human validation of two automated judges, invalid-answer analysis, hyperparameter-selection summaries, and decomposition of harmful versus beneficial entanglement. These address reliability and interpretation questions not analyzed in v1 (Appendices E.2, E.6, G.1, G.3, and G.4).

E5.justification: V1's heatmap asterisks identify target datasets, not statistical significance. V3 introduces paired t-tests with FDR correction by steering objective and significance markers throughout the result heatmaps, plus Cohen's kappa estimates for human–judge agreement. These are substantial additions to statistical reporting, without establishing additional seeds or repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive model, morality-steering, long-context, and validation results. For example, Figure 10 reports a 21.2-point morality improvement from PCA steering on Llama. Existing entries also change: Qwen's DIM refusal-steering morality delta changes from −10.7 points in v1 Figure 3 to −15.5 in v3 Figure 13, alongside a changed baseline. TwinViews results are replaced under revised scoring, so they are not same-protocol performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes entanglement from sqrt(sum of squared shifts)/n to sqrt(sum of squared shifts/n), a mathematically different normalization. Appendix G.1 adds signed harmful and beneficial components with the identity Entanglement² = Harm² + Benef². These are limited mathematical additions and corrections; the expanded steering formulas mainly document existing procedures.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a broad entanglement benchmark and a modular evaluation framework, with steering dependent on the method–model–target combination. V3's abstract and conclusion add specific claims about social-behavior vulnerability, morality degradation from refusal suppression, and opposing political shifts across models. These sharpen the empirical claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: V1's brief representation-geometry and shared-prompt-mechanism discussion becomes an extensive account of method-specific hypotheses and feature superposition, explicitly distinguished from causal findings (v3 Sections 4.2 and 5). V3 also adds substantive qualifications about refusal-direction asymmetry, conditional-gating failures, political-view scoring, judge reliability, and transfer to deployment settings.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands v1's short implementation appendix with exact negative-answer and judge prompts, CAA/RepE templates, direction-extraction details, selected layers and coefficients, conditional thresholds, decoding settings, hardware, software, and compute estimates (Appendices B–F; Tables 5–13). These largely disclose previously unspecified details rather than demonstrate changes to the original procedures.

R1.justification: V3 adds literature connecting entanglement to fine-tuning, RLHF, and sycophancy, including Hawkins et al. and Malmqvist, while removing discussion of LEACE, iterative nullspace projection, and Im and Li's steering evaluation. The central positioning relative to AxBench, EasyEdit2, and modular representation-steering frameworks remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively rewritten and reorganized: the title and benchmark terminology change, related work moves before the benchmark, detailed methodology and limitations move into appendices, and results are structured around explicit findings, tradeoffs, and scale consistency. A dedicated interpretive section replaces much briefer discussion.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main layout, replaces the dataset sunburst with a taxonomy-and-examples diagram, and introduces perspective-specific effectiveness, entanglement, and tradeoff plots. Heatmaps reorder columns, add morality-steering blocks and significance annotations, and expand to additional models. Numerous new tables present validation, hyperparameters, decomposition, errors, and long-context results.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential reliability and reproducibility. It addresses v1's TwinViews formatting confound, validates two automated judges, distinguishes harmful from beneficial drift, and supplies statistical testing and detailed implementation information. Broader model and context checks further test the findings' scope. DarkBench validation remains borrowed from prior work and seed-level variability is uncharacterized, but the revisions resolve several important measurement and documentation weaknesses.
